Test-only change; the reordering is correct and fixes a real flake. Root cause confirmed in Subnet.validate_cidr (src/maasserver/models/subnet.py:454-474): any new subnet overlapping an existing one is rejected globally. Previously make_RackController() ran first and generated a random IPv4 subnet (/24-/28 prefix, make_ip4_or_6_network -> make_ipv4_network); whenever its first octet was 10 it overlapped 10.0.0.0/8, and the later make_Subnet(cidr="10.0.0.0/8") - directly or via make_StaticIPAddress(cidr=...) - raised "Subnet ... would overlap with existing subnets" (~1/256 per affected test). Creating the pinned subnet first and threading it through make_RackController(subnet=...) and make_StaticIPAddress(subnet=...) leaves exactly one subnet per test: make_Node_with_Interface_on_Subnet uses vlan = subnet.vlan, creates the boot interface there with interface_count=1, and no random subnet is generated. The Discovery DB view (src/maasserver/testing/initial.maas_test.sql:5260-5296) joins on vlan.id = subnet.vlan_id AND neigh.ip << subnet.cidr, so test_associates_known_subnet and test_is_external_dhcp still exercise the intended association/is_external_dhcp paths.

I also checked the non-obvious consequence of creating the subnet before the first assertion: make_Subnet keeps gateway_ip at first+1 (10.0.0.1) and does not create a StaticIPAddress for the gateway, while the rack's auto-created rows have ip="", so by_unknown_ip still returns 1 before the explicit StaticIPAddress is added.

Nit: test_does_not_fail_if_cannot_find_subnet (untouched) still gets a random subnet on its interface VLAN; it cannot hit the overlap failure (no pinned CIDR is created), and the assertion would only break if that random subnet actually contained 10.0.0.1 (negligible), so no action required - but pinning a subnet and using an IP outside it would make it fully deterministic too.

Nit: the 3-line setup is now duplicated six times; a small local helper would keep the copies from drifting. Verification here was static (factory/model/DB-view inspection); no test runner or DB was available in this environment.

src/maasserver/api/tests/test_discoverie.130: make_RackController(subnet=subnet) already records the interface created on that subnet as node.boot_interface (make_Node_with_Interface_on_Subnet, src/maasserver/testing/factory.py:1158-1168). current_config.interface_set.first() relies on there being exactly one interface and on unordered-queryset ordering, and would silently pick a different NIC if make_Controller ever creates a second interface. rack.boot_interface (or rack.get_boot_interface()) states the intent, is what the factory guarantees here, and saves a query. Same for line 143.

src/maasserver/models/tests/test_discove.80: Same suggestion as the API tests: prefer rack.boot_interface over current_config.interface_set.first(). The factory explicitly points boot_interface at the interface it created on the subnet passed to make_RackController, whereas .first() depends on interface count and ordering. Applies to lines 44, 55, 80 and 87.
